summary: Spread across 21 square miles at a density of just 243 people per square mile, Yosemite Lakes is less a traditional town and more a scattering of foothill parcels along the Highway 41 corridor northeast of Fresno, sitting at the lower edge of the Sierra Nevada foothills roughly 15 miles south of the entrance to Yosemite National Park. That proximity is the headline — but daily life looks nothing like a national-park gateway; this is a census-designated place without a conventional downtown, commercial strip, or walkable center, meaning nearly every errand involves a car trip toward Oakhurst or down to Fresno. The median home value of roughly $354,000 against a median household income just above $100,000 yields a price-to-income ratio around 3.5 — relatively manageable by California standards — yet median rent at $2,204 eats a substantial share of that same income for non-owners. Employment skews toward tourism, forestry-adjacent services, and healthcare facilities clustered in Oakhurst and Madera County, making this firmly a bedroom community with limited local job switching. Annual highs averaging 74°F and nearly 9.5 hours of daily sunshine deliver golden-grass summers and mild winters, though elevation means cooler nights than the valley floor. The defining tradeoff is stark: spectacular Sierra access purchased at the cost of meaningful isolation from urban services and employment centers.
